scope_notes: Warm/cold remain separate. Cold means store drop/reopen before each append, not OS page-cache eviction.

append_ns brackets append_canonical only. Cold operation CPU/write brackets exclude reopen but include process-sample overhead. append_phase counters include reopen and sampling; both are reported separately.
100-Hz counters mean 10ms ticks; per-append cold brackets are coarse and sums of separately rounded brackets can amplify quantization. Zero is preserved, not interpreted as CPU-free work.
Full lifecycle includes initialization/history seeding/append/reopen verification/cleanup. Absolute through-cleanup counters and start-to-end deltas are separately named.
max_sampled memory uses lifecycle endpoints to match prior reports. max_all_observed memory additionally includes every cold operation endpoint. Both are sampled maxima, not actual peaks.

Missing/invalid counters are retained with reasons, partial memory maxima stay partial, and ratios with zero denominators remain undefined. Summaries retain pair positions and explicitly report available/required counts.
Outliers, zero values and adverse observations are never trimmed. Medians are medians of matched pair ratios, never ratios of unpaired medians.

Manifest paths are retained historical identity data. Actual binary files are verified only in strict mode; archive mode can recompute raw data without original host files and explicitly reports that actual binaries were not checked. No current HEAD is consulted.

Product accepted/oracle/test-log fields verify retained assertions; this script cannot independently recover the deleted original databases or prove runtime isolation. Per-product records do not contain argv, so executable binding relies on the retained cohort manifest.
No performance attribution is assigned to individual source changes. Three pairs do not establish parity or population nonregression.
